exhibits.titleSi: Napoleonova carinarnica — Griblje v Ilirskih provincah (1809–1813)
exhibits.titleEn: Napoleon's customs post — Griblje in the Illyrian Provinces (1809–1813)
exhibits.periodSi: 1809–1813 · francoska uprava · carinski urad inšpektorata Sisek
exhibits.periodEn: 1809–1813 · French administration · customs office of the Sisak inspectorate
exhibits.summarySi: V letih Ilirskih provinc so Francozi ob Kolpi postavili verigo carinarnic — med njimi tudi v Gribljah: urad inšpektorata Sisek med Metliko, Vinico in Brodom ob Kolpi. Kratek, a resničen pridelek Napoleonovega imperija na robu vasi.
exhibits.summaryEn: In the years of the Illyrian Provinces the French placed a chain of customs posts along the Kolpa — among them one at Griblje: an office of the Sisak inspectorate between Metlika, Vinica and Brod ob Kolpi. A short but true crop of Napoleon's empire at the edge of the village.
exhibits.storySi:
Med Valvasorjevim zapisom iz leta 1689 in šolsko dobo iz leta 1885 je v tej zbirki stoletja, ki se zdijo tiha. Eno od njih je zdaj dobilo glas: med letoma 1809 in 1813, ko so po Dunajskem miru dežele od Zgornje Kranjske do Dalmacije sestavljale francoske Ilirske province, je bil konec napoleonske uprave tudi v Gribljah — in sicer v obliki, ki jo ta vas pozna najbolje: kot mejna postaja.

Seznam carinskih uradov Ilirije, ki ga navaja članek o Ilirskih provincah (po literaturi, med drugim po razpravah Jelke Pivec Stele iz leta 1930), našteva za inšpektorat Sisek vrsto mest ob meji s Turškim cesarstvom: Sisek, Krško, Karlovec, Metlika, most pri Metliki — in naprej ob Kolpi: Griblje, Pobrežje, Vinica, Poljane, Brod ob Kolpi, Osilnica, Lož. Med njimi je Griblje manjše od vseh — a na seznamu stoji z enakim pomenom: kraj, kjer se preverja blago, prehode in ljudi.

Za vas ob Kolpi to ni prva in ne zadnja mejna služba. Uskoška vojna krajina je tu vpregla zemljo v obrambo stoletja prej; habsburška Meja je pozneje nosila svojo žandarmerijo in železnico, ki je vasi srečno obšla; po letu 1991 je Kolpa postala zunanja meja samostojne Slovenije, po Schengnu pa se je spet odprla. Napoleonova carinarnica je najkrajše poglavje te zgodbe — komaj štiri leta — a ravno dolžina jo dela muzejsko: dokaz, da so imperiji, ki so si delili Evropo, vsakič znova potrebovali isti prehod: prečkanje Kolpe pri Gribljah.

Napoleonska doba v Gribljah pa ne ostaja samo na papirju — ima svoj predmet. V kulturnozgodovinski zbirki Belokranjskega muzeja v Metliki hranijo toaletno skledico iz porcelana s kolorirano podobo cesarja Napoleona I. v sredini — začetek 19. stoletja, kraj predmeta: Griblje, inventarna številka 1767. Takšne predmete so na belokranjske police prinesle Ilirske province (1809–1813); Francozi sami — z uvedbo in izterjavo višjih davkov — med prebivalci niso bili priljubljeni: v Starem trgu in Črnomlju se je uprlo, zato je morala priti vojska iz Novega mesta. Skledica je prvi znani muzejsko hranjeni predmet te zgodbe: dokaz, da napoleonska prisotnost pri Gribljah ni bila samo vrstica v carinskem seznamu, ampak tudi stvar, ki je prišla v vaško hišo — in v Beli krajini ostala.

Ilirske province so zapustile tudi zemljevid: leta 1812 so francoski geometri zarisali njihove meje na karti, ki jo je ZRC SAZU obnovil v knjigi Zemljevid Ilirskih provinc iz leta 1812. Na njej Griblje samodejno ne piše — bile so prevelike črte za tako majhno vas; ta zapis pa jo prvič postavlja na lastno karto.
exhibits.storyEn:
Between Valvasor's entry of 1689 and the school era of 1885, this collection holds centuries that seem silent. One of them has now found a voice: between 1809 and 1813, when the lands from Upper Carniola to Dalmatia formed the French Illyrian Provinces after the Peace of Schönbrunn, the reach of Napoleonic administration touched Griblje too — and in the form this village knows best: as a border station.

The list of Illyrian customs offices, given in the article on the Illyrian Provinces (following the literature, among them Pivec Stele's 1930 studies), enumerates for the Sisak inspectorate a series of places along the border with the Ottoman Empire: Sisak, Krško, Karlovac, Metlika, the bridge at Metlika — and on along the Kolpa: Griblje, Pobrežje, Vinica, Poljane, Brod ob Kolpi, Osilnica, Lož. Among them Griblje is smaller than all — but it stands on the list with the same meaning: a place where goods, crossings and people are checked.

For a village on the Kolpa this is neither the first nor the last border duty. The Uskok Military Frontier had harnessed this land to defence centuries earlier; the Habsburg Border later carried its gendarmerie and the railway that happily bypassed the village; after 1991 the Kolpa became the external border of independent Slovenia, and after Schengen it opened again. Napoleon's customs post is the shortest chapter of that story — barely four years — and precisely its length makes it museum material: proof that the empires that divided Europe needed, again and again, the same crossing on the Kolpa at Griblje.

The Napoleonic years at Griblje, however, do not remain on paper alone — they have an object. In the cultural-history collection of the Bela krajina Museum in Metlika a porcelain toilet basin is kept, bearing a coloured portrait of Emperor Napoleon I at its centre — early 19th century, place of the object: Griblje, inventory number 1767. Objects of this kind were brought onto Bela krajina shelves by the Illyrian Provinces (1809–1813); the French themselves — imposing and collecting higher taxes — were unpopular among the people: Stari trg and Črnomelj rose in revolt, and the army from Novo mesto had to put it down. The basin is the first known museum-kept object of this story: proof that the Napoleonic presence at Griblje was not only a line in the customs list, but a thing that came into a village house — and stayed in Bela krajina.

The Illyrian Provinces also left a map: in 1812 French surveyors drew their borders on a chart that ZRC SAZU restored in the book The Map of the Illyrian Provinces of 1812. On it Griblje does not appear — the lines were too large for so small a village; this record places it on a map of its own for the first time.

exhibits.titleSi: Tone Kralj — devetindevetdeset pomladi
exhibits.titleEn: Tone Kralj — ninety-nine springs and counting
exhibits.summarySi: Januarja 2026 je Tone Kralj iz Gribelj praznoval 98. rojstni dan: še pobira in lušči lešnike, suši peteršilj, rešuje križanke in karta s pravnuki. Obiskali so ga Rdeči križ, borci za vrednote NOB in upokojenci Črnomlja.
exhibits.summaryEn: In January 2026 Tone Kralj of Griblje celebrated his 98th birthday: he still gathers and shells hazelnuts, dries parsley, solves crosswords and plays cards with his great-grandchildren. The Red Cross, the veterans of NOB values and the Črnomelj pensioners came to visit.
exhibits.storySi:
Ta zapis je najmlajši v zbirki — nastal je januarja 2026, ko je Tone Kralj iz Gribelj praznoval osemindevetdeseti rojstni dan in stopil v devetindevetdeseto pomlad. Povabilo so sprejeli predstavniki Območnega združenja Rdečega križa Črnomelj, Združenja borcev za vrednote NOB Bele krajine in Društva upokojencev Črnomelj; slavljenca in njegovo družino so, kot piše vir, »lepo sprejeli ob polni mizi dobrot«.

Kaj pa ta zapis dela v muzeju, ki sicer hrani pet tisoč let stare črepinje? Njegovo gradivo je namreč iz najredkejše zbirke: vsakdan, ki ga običajno nihče ne dokumentira. Pri osemindevetdesetih letih Tone še pomaga pri pobiranju in luščenju lešnikov ter pri sušenju in shranjevanju peteršilja; v prostem času rešuje križanke, bere časopis in karta s pravnuki. Vsak od teh gibov je majhna zmaga nad časom — in vsak je hkrati droben arheološki dokument gribeljskega letnega kroga: lešnik ob robu gozda, zelišče z vrta, karte pri mizi.

Griblje imajo s stoletniki svojo zgodovino: Nikolaj Dragoš, rojen v vasi leta 1907, je bil najstarejši Slovenec svojega časa in je sto let dočakal med tamburami. Tone Kralj tej stopnici počasi stopa naproti. Muzej zato ta zapis razume kot začetek: če ga bo januarja 2028 lahko dopolnil s stoletnico, bo zapis zrasel iz novice v praznovanje. Do takrat pa naj ostane, kar je: dokaz, da se v Gribljah leta ne samo štejejo — se tudi živijo.

Dolenjski list je Kraljev mejnik zapisal že osem let prej: februarja 2018 je ob devetdesetem rojstnem dnevu objavil zgodbo »90 let Antona Kralja iz Gribelj — od kurirčka«. Te tri besede — od kurirčka — so najzgodnejši znani poklicni zapis o Kralju: deček iz Gribelj, ki je med vojno nosil sporočila, je praznoval devetdeseto in nato devetindevetdeseto pomlad.
exhibits.storyEn:
This is the youngest record in the collection — it was made in January 2026, when Tone Kralj of Griblje celebrated his ninety-eighth birthday. The invitation was accepted by representatives of the Črnomelj Red Cross, the Association of Fighters for the Values of the National Liberation Struggle of Bela krajina, and the Črnomelj Pensioners' Society; the celebrant and his family, as the source says, "kindly received them at a full table of delicacies".

And what is such a record doing in a museum that otherwise keeps five-thousand-year-old potsherds? Its material comes from the rarest collection of all: the everyday that no one usually documents. At ninety-eight, Tone still helps with gathering and shelling hazelnuts and with drying and storing parsley; in his free time he solves crosswords, reads the paper and plays cards with his great-grandchildren. Each of these movements is a small victory over time — and each is also a tiny archaeological document of the Griblje farming year: the hazel at the forest edge, the herb from the garden, the cards at the table.

Griblje has a history with centenarians: Nikolaj Dragoš, born in the village in 1907, was the oldest Slovene of his time and reached a hundred years among the tamburas. Tone Kralj is quietly preparing to follow his staircase. The museum therefore reads this record as a beginning: if in January 2028 it can be enlarged with a hundredth birthday, the record will grow from news into celebration. Until then, let it remain what it is: proof that in Griblje years are not only counted — they are lived.

Dolenjski list recorded Kralj's milestone eight years earlier: in February 2018, on his ninetieth birthday, it published the story »90 let Antona Kralja iz Gribelj — od kurirčka« ('Anton Kralj of Griblje is 90 — from a little courier'). Those three words — od kurirčka — are the earliest known calling on record for Kralj: the boy from Griblje who carried messages in the war went on to celebrate his ninetieth and then his ninety-eighth spring.

exhibits.titleSi: Kupski manevri 1937 — vojaška postaja za pitno vodo pri Gribljih
exhibits.titleEn: The Kupa manoeuvres of 1937 — the army's drinking-water station at Griblje
exhibits.periodSi: september 1937 · Kraljevina Jugoslavija · vaje ob reki Kupi
exhibits.periodEn: September 1937 · Kingdom of Yugoslavia · the exercises on the Kupa river
exhibits.summarySi: Septembra 1937 so potekali kupski manevri — največji mirnodopski vojaški dogodek Kraljevine Jugoslavije. Za oskrbo okrog 20.000 vojakov je vojska na področju Bele in Suhe krajine uredila posebne postaje za pročiščevanje pitne vode; ena od petih je bila v Gribljah.
exhibits.summaryEn: In September 1937 the Kupa manoeuvres took place — the largest peacetime military event of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. To supply some 20,000 soldiers the army built special drinking-water treatment stations in Bela and Suha krajina; one of the five stood at Griblje.
exhibits.storySi:
Septembra 1937 se je pokrajina ob Kolpi za nekaj tednov spremenila v vojaški poligon. Kupski manevri — največji mirnodopski dogodek vojske Kraljevine Jugoslavije — so združili dve manevarski skupini: številčnejšo »rdečo« na severu, sestavljeno večinoma iz enot Dravske divizijske oblasti, in manjšo »belo« na hrvaškem tlu. Na slovensko stran je prišlo okrog 20.000 vojakov s konji, vozovi in mostovnimi ekipami; k vajam je sodila tudi logistika — ceste, oskrba, poljske kuhinje in voda.

Prav voda je postala logistična nit, ki je zašla tudi v Griblje. Vojska je na področju Bele in Suhe krajine morala organizirati posebne postaje za pročiščevanje pitne vode: v vaseh Sveta Marija, Gradac, Dvor, Vinica in Griblje. Tako je gribeljska ravnica za nekaj tednov nosila vojaško infrastrukturo, ki je oskrbovala tisoče ust — vas, navajena potokov, studencev in malence, se je za mesec dni uvrstila na vojaške zemljevide kot pipa za dvajset tisoč ljudi.

Za vas je bil to dogodek s predzgodbo in nadaljevanjem. Vojska je tu stala stoletja prej kot obmejna krajina; po aprilu 1941 je mejna policija na cesti v Gribljah pripeljala vojaški svet nazaj v vas; štiri leta po manevrih, 6. septembra 1941, se je na isti cesti zgodila zaseda — prva oborožena akcija belokranjskih partizanov. V tem zaporedju so manevri 1937 zadnji mirnodopski vojaški pečat na gribeljski ravnici: še vaje, ne še vojna.

Zapis temelji na znanstveni študiji o kupskih manevrih, ki je leta 2025 izšla v Časopisu za suvremenu povijest in stoji na arhivski podlagi vojaških in banovinskih spisov. Muzej išče: fotografije vojakov pri Gribljih leta 1937, spomine domačinov na manevre in natančno mesto vodne postaje — vsak od teh dokumentov bo zapis iz splošne vojaške zgodovine približal vaški.
exhibits.storyEn:
In September 1937 the landscape along the Kolpa turned into a military training ground for a few weeks. The Kupa manoeuvres — the largest peacetime event of the Army of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia — joined two manoeuvre groups: the more numerous "red" one in the north, formed mostly of units of the Drava divisional district, and the smaller "white" one on Croatian soil. Some 20,000 soldiers with horses, carts and bridging units came to the Slovene side; the exercises included logistics as well — roads, supply, field kitchens and water.

Water became the logistic thread that also led to Griblje. In Bela and Suha krajina the army had to organise special drinking-water treatment stations: in the villages of Sveta Marija, Gradac, Dvor, Vinica and Griblje. For a few weeks the Griblje plain thus carried military infrastructure serving thousands of mouths — a village used to streams, springs and weirs entered the military maps for a month as the tap for twenty thousand people.

For the village this was an event with a prehistory and a sequel. The army had stood here centuries earlier as the frontier landscape; after April 1941 the border police on the Griblje road brought the military world back to the village; four years after the manoeuvres, on 6 September 1941, the ambush happened on the same road — the first armed action of Bela krajina's Partisans. In that sequence the 1937 manoeuvres were the last peacetime military imprint on the Griblje plain: still exercises, not yet war.

The record rests on a scholarly study of the Kupa manoeuvres published in 2025 in the journal Časopis za suvremenu povijest, grounded in military and provincial archives. The museum is looking for: photographs of soldiers at Griblje in 1937, villagers' memories of the manoeuvres and the exact site of the water station — each such document will bring the record from general military history closer to the village.

Tako se i na slovenskom tlu osigurala lokalna opskrba pitkom vodom za još oko 20.000 vojnika tijekom Kupskih manevara.«

exhibits.titleSi: Bronasta igla iz Gribelj — predmet z inventarno številko A 478
exhibits.titleEn: The bronze pin from Griblje — an object with inventory number A 478
exhibits.periodSi: pozna bronasta doba (tipološka umestitev) · predmet objavljen 1979
exhibits.periodEn: Late Bronze Age (typological placement) · the object published in 1979
exhibits.summarySi: V objavi žarnega grobišča na Borštku pri Metliki (1979) je z lokacijo »Griblje« zapisana bronasta igla s profilirano glavico (inv. št. A 478, 19,6 cm) — prvi imenovani predmet iz Gribelj, objavljen v arheološki literaturi.
exhibits.summaryEn: In the publication of the urn necropolis at Boršt near Metlika (1979) a bronze pin with a profiled head is listed under the place-name "Griblje" (inv. no. A 478, 19.6 cm) — the first named object from Griblje published in the archaeological literature.
exhibits.storySi:
Arheološka zgodba Gribelj ne živi samo pod njivami ob Kolpi — živi tudi v inventarjih muzejev. V objavi žarnega grobišča na Borštku v Metliki, ki jo je leta 1979 v Arheološkem vestniku objavil Janez Dular, med gradivom stoji zapis, ki je za ta muzej nenavadno dragocen: »Bronasta igla s profilirano glavico Griblje (A 478); velikost 19,6 cm« (t. 12: 5).

Igla s profilirano glavico je predmet, ki spada v izročilje pozne bronaste in zgodnje železne dobe — sveta žarnih grobišč in prvih knežjih središč, kakršno je Boršt nad Metliko. Dolga skoraj dvajset centimetrov, je pripadala oprsju ali pričeski — in v Dularjevi objavi stoji ob grobnih pridatkih Boršta kot primerjava, ki dokazuje, da je gribeljska najdba tipološko sodila v isti svet metliških žarnih grobov. V rokah je nosila isti čas, v katerem so ob Kolpi zrastle naselbine, ki jih muzej predstavlja v zapisu o najdišču ob Kolpi.

Kje je predmet danes? Številčenje »A« je oblika, ki v slovenski arheologiji kaže na arheološko zbirko Narodnega muzeja Slovenije — vendar točen dom predmeta, kontekst najdbe (kdaj in kje v Gribljih) ter natančno datiranje čakajo na pregled inventarjev. Muzej to vrzel izrecno zapisuje, namesto da bi jo zapolnil z domnevo; objava iz leta 1979 je doslej trdni dokaz, da predmet obstaja.

To je prvi imenovani predmet iz Gribelj, objavljen v arheološki literaturi — in hkrati manjkajoč člen med pokrajino pod vasjo ter zbirki, ki jo hranijo muzeji. Muzej išče: fotografijo igle, karton najdbe in potrditev hrambe; vsak od teh dokumentov bo predmetu vrnil ime kraja, ki ga nosi.
exhibits.storyEn:
The archaeological story of Griblje does not live only beneath the fields by the Kolpa — it also lives in museum inventories. In the publication of the urn necropolis at Boršt in Metlika, which Janez Dular published in 1979 in Arheološki vestnik, there stands among the material a line of unusual value for this museum: "A bronze pin with a profiled head, Griblje (A 478); size 19.6 cm" (pl. 12: 5).

A pin with a profiled head belongs to the legacy of the Late Bronze and Early Iron Age — the world of urn necropolises and the first princely centres, such as Boršt above Metlika. Almost twenty centimetres long, it belonged to dress or hairstyle; in Dular's publication it stands beside the grave goods of Boršt as a comparison proving that the Griblje find belonged typologically to the same world as the Metlika urn graves. In hand it carried the same age in which the settlements along the Kolpa grew, the ones this museum presents in its record of the site by the Kolpa.

Where is the object today? The "A" numbering is a form that in Slovene archaeology points to the archaeological collection of the National Museum of Slovenia — yet the object's exact home, the find context (when and where in Griblje) and its precise dating await an examination of the inventories. The museum records this gap openly instead of filling it with conjecture; the 1979 publication is, so far, the firm proof that the object exists.

This is the first named object from Griblje published in the archaeological literature — and at the same time the missing link between the landscape beneath the village and the collections kept by museums. The museum is looking for: a photograph of the pin, the find card and confirmation of its keeping; every one of these documents will return to the object the name of the place it carries.

exhibits.titleSi: Kolpa se zavije pri Gribljih — prikrito prečanje čez reko 1941–1943
exhibits.titleEn: The Kolpa bends at Griblje — the secret crossing of the river, 1941–1943
exhibits.summarySi: Pri ovinku Kolpe pri Gribljih italijanska straža ni imela pregleda — in prav tam so hrvaški kajdarji prikrivajoče prevažali ljudi čez reko, med njimi begunce in Žide s hrvaške strani. Pričevanje soseda iz Krasinca o slepem mestu obmejnega pasu, ki je postalo prehod.
exhibits.summaryEn: At the bend of the Kolpa at Griblje the Italian sentries had no view — and right there Croatian boatmen secretly ferried people across the river, among them refugees and Jews from the Croatian side. The testimony of a neighbour from Krasinec about the blind spot of the border zone that became a passage.
exhibits.storySi:
Meje niso vidne le na zemljevidu — vidne so tudi s stražarskega mesta. Jožef Klepec iz Krasinca je v intervjuju za razstavo Inštituta za novejšo zgodovino o okupacijskih mejah povedal, kako je izgledala reka s strani tistih, ki so jo stražili: »Italijani so tu imeli stražo. Gor in dol od nas kak kilometer je Kolpa ravna, pri Gribljah pa malo zavije, tam Italijani niso imeli pregleda.«

Ovinka, kjer se reka ukrivi in stran odteče od stražarjevega očesa, je postal prehod. »Nekateri hrvaški državljani so tam Žide vozili čez vodo,« je povedal Klepec. Med prečkanimi so bili begunci in Židi s hrvaške strani; »ljudje so pripovedovali, da so bili bogati« — in tudi pohlep je naredil svoj del: »Okradli so jih ti, ki so jih vozili čez Kolpo. Ko so prišli na drugo stran reke, so kričali, da so Italijani, bejžmo, bejžmo. Židi so poskakali ven, oni pa s čolnom, polnim robe, nazaj na hrvaško stran.« Reka je bila hkrati pot in past; pričevanje ne polepšava — pripoveduje oboje.

Klepecov spomin shrani še drobec vaške vojne ekonomije: »Židi so nosili s seboj prtljago, drugače pa so imeli v glavnem denar — zlato, cekine. Spominjam se, ko sem še v šolo hodil, da sta šla oče in mati na Hrvaško kupit te cekine, da so jih nato nosili zobarom. To je bilo kvalitetno zlato … cela dolina si je s temi cekini zobe delala.« Zlatniki, preneseni čez reko pri Gribljih, so se v naslednjih letih pretakali po hišah doline — pričevanje o tem, kako vojna prestavi vrednote: kje je zlato, kadar svet gori.

Za ta muzej je ovinka pri Gribljih zapis o vasi, ki v vojni ni bila le prizorišče postojanke in zasede (zapis zaseda-1941) — bila je tudi slepo mesto obmejnega pasu: detajl pokrajine, v katerem je umikala vrzel dovolj velika, da je čeznjo šlo človeško življenje. Muzej išče: imena kajdarjev, ki so prevažali, zgodbe družin, ki so prečale, in spomine obeh bregov — pričevanje je prvo stran te knjige, listov je še veliko.
exhibits.storyEn:
Borders are visible not only on maps — they are visible from the sentry's post too. Jožef Klepec of Krasinec, interviewed for the Institute of Contemporary History's exhibition on the occupation borders, described how the river looked from the side of those who guarded it: "The Italians had sentries here. About a kilometre up and down from our village the Kolpa River flows straight, but near Griblje it takes a turn and the Italians couldn't see there."

The bend where the river curves away from the watchman's eye became a passage. "Certain Croatian citizens ferried Jews across the water there," Klepec recalled. Among those ferried were refugees and Jews from the Croatian side; "the people said that the Jews were rich" — and greed took its share too: "They were robbed by the people ferrying them across the Kolpa River. When they reached the opposite bank, they started yelling that the Italians had come, run, run. The Jews jumped out and they took the boat, full of goods, back to the Croatian side." The river was at once a road and a trap; the testimony does not embellish — it tells both.

Klepec's memory also preserves a fragment of the village's wartime economy: "The Jews carried luggage with them, but they mostly had money — gold, gold coins. I remember when I was still in school that my father and mother went to Croatia to buy those coins, to take them afterwards to the barbers. It was good quality gold ... the whole valley was making its teeth shine with those coins." Gold coins carried across the river at Griblje flowed through the houses of the valley in the years that followed — a testimony of how war displaces value: where does gold live when the world burns.

For this museum the bend at Griblje is a record of a village that in the war was not only the site of a post and an ambush (see the ambush record) — it was also the blind spot of the border zone: a detail of the landscape in which a gap opened wide enough for a human life to cross it. The museum is looking for: the names of the boatmen who ferried, the stories of the families who crossed, and the memories of both banks — the testimony is the first page of that book; many pages remain.

exhibits.titleSi: Javna razsvetljava 2023 — luč, pod katero je kopala arheologija
exhibits.titleEn: The 2023 public lighting — the light beneath which archaeology dug
exhibits.periodEn: July – early October 2023 · Municipality of Črnomelj
exhibits.summarySi: Zaključena izgradnja javne razsvetljave v Gribljih: okrog 70.000 evrov občine in okrog 7.000 evrov krajanov — z arheološkimi raziskavami ob gradnji, vrednimi okrog 12.500 evrov, ki so v vaško modernizacijo vpisale tudi preteklost. Dve leti pozneje po istem vzorcu asfaltiranih 190 metrov vaške poti.
exhibits.summaryEn: The completion of Griblje's public lighting: some €70,000 from the municipality and some €7,000 from the villagers — with archaeological surveys during the construction, worth about €12,500, writing the past into the village's modernisation. Two years later, by the same pattern, 190 metres of the village road were asphalted.
exhibits.storySi:
Zima v Beli krajini teme nikoli ne odpusti, vas pa se je dolgo svetila po lastni presoji — luč pri hiši, fenjer pri cesti. Leta 2023 je ta red zamenjala javna razsvetljava: dela podjetja EVI iz Črnomlja so potekala od julija do konca avgusta, občina Črnomelj je vložila okrog 70.000 evrov, krajani pa s prostovoljnimi prispevki — že uveljavljeno vaško lastnostjo — dodali okrog 7.000 evrov. Svetlobo so uradno odprli ob koncu tedna v začetku oktobra, s kulturnim programom; nagovora župana Andreja Kavška in predsednice KS Romane Husič sta potrdila, kar je dokazalo že prejšnja leta: vaška infrastruktura je roman, ki ga pišeta občina in vas skupaj.

V zapisu o svetlobi pa je najtežji podatek najtišji: ob izgradnji so bile izvedene arheološke raziskave, vredne okrog 12.500 evrov. Vas, pod katero ležijo keltsko zlato Pezdirčeve njive in najdišča ob Kolpi, danes ne kopa več po slepo — vsak jarok, ki vzame lopato, najprej vpraša arheologe. Rezultati teh raziskav javnosti še niso znani — muzej jih izrecno išče, kar pečat zaradi skromnega obsega gradnje še povečuje: redki so primeri, ko bi tako majhna vaška investicija sploh znesla arheološki nadzor.

Dva leta pozneje, avgusta 2025, je bil po enakem vzorcu sodelovanja na novo asfaltiran najbolj poškodovan odsek javne poti — 190 metrov, okrog 35.000 evrov: občina za asfalt, krajevna skupnost za zamenjavo podlage. Zaporedje — zvonovi, šola, razsvetljava, cesta — je koledar vasi, ki si svoj svet uredi sama: po vrstici in po letu.

Zaporedje ima predzgodovino, ki jo je Radio Odeon zapisal štiriindvajset mesecev prej: jeseni 2021 je ista kombinacija zažarala zaselek Brinsko selo. Dela je znova izvedel EVI iz Črnomlja, znova je sodelovala arheologija — tokrat Skupina STIK iz Ljubljane, strošek 11.931,60 evrov ob investiciji 46.987,81 evrov —, znova so sredstva zbrale obe strani (krajani in KS Griblje 10.000 evrov, ostalo občina), in znova je bila predaja namenu slovesnost treh imen: župan Andrej Kavšek, predsednik KS Toni Brinc — danes član sveta, takrat na čelu — in dobrotnik dr. Franc Brinc. Dva projekta, dve leti razlike, en vzorec: vas in občina svetita z istim potpisom.

Tok ima tudi svoje vsakdanje zapise, ki jih kronika redko hrani: decembra 2021 je Elektro Ljubljana (distribucijska enota Novo mesto, nadzorništvo Metlika) zaradi del na distribucijskem omrežju za dve uri izklopila transformatorsko postajo GOR. GRIBLJE — brez toka je ostalo dvajset naslovov, hišne številke 3–15 z razdelki A in B ter en naslov zapisan kar kot »BŠ«. Rutinsko obvestilo je v resnici redka dokumentirana mikro-geografija vaškega omrežja: pove, katera okna si delijo isti kabel — podatek, ki ga muzejska kronika sicer ne piše, arhivi elektrodistribucije pa ga hranijo le v tehniških skicah.

Infrastrukturni koledar vasi ima starejšo stran: 5. septembra 2008 je Dolenjski list zapisal »Iz Gribelj nič več v Kolpo« — odprtje čistilne naprave ob Kolpi in nove kanalizacije za 200–300 populacijskih enot, naložbe iz dobrega milijona evrov, za katero je evropski protokol zahteval predstavitev prav v gasilskem domu; 70 % sredstev je prispelo iz EU, župan Andrej Fabjan pa je projekt pozdravil kot prispevek k čistejši Kolpi. Čistilna naprava 2008, javna razsvetljava 2023, asfalt 2025 — enak vzorec tri generacije zapored: vas, ki srečo gradi po koščkih.

Od leta 2025 pa je zgodba dobila tudi natančno mapa omrežja, ki jo pišejo izklopi: oktobra 2025 je Elektro Ljubljana na en potez odrezala TP GOR. GRIBLJE — kar 38 naslovov, od GRIBLJE 1 A do 52 in BŠ; junija 2026 je sledil izklop izvoda 2, ki ga je Elektro poimenovala kar sama: »GOR.G.-VIKENDI« (naslovi 1 A, 4 A, 4 G, 25 D in BŠ) — vikend hiše ob Kolpi; avgusta 2026 pa je tok izginil še z izvoda Šola postaje TP GRIBLJE (30 A–48 in BŠ) — dokaz, da ima vas poleg GOR. GRIBLJE še drugo transformatorsko postajo, njen krak ob šoli pa lastno ime. Vsak izklop je nesramen, a nenadomestljiv popis: pove, katera okna si delijo isti kabel — zdaj vemo, da jih delijo po dveh postajah in vsaj treh poimenovanih krakih. Razsvetljava blizu šole pa ima svoj datum rojstva: trak sta ga 8. oktobra 2021 presekala dr. Franc Brinc in predsednik KS Toni Brinc ob županu Andreju Kavšku.

Muzej išče: rezultate arheoloških raziskav ob izgradnji razsvetljave, fotografijo odprtja in popis prve javne svetilke v vasi — kje je gorela, preden je prišel tok.
exhibits.storyEn:
Winter in Bela krajina never forgives the dark, and for long the village lit itself by its own judgement — a lamp by the house, a lantern by the road. In 2023 that order was replaced by public lighting: the works of the Črnomelj firm EVI ran from July to the end of August, the Municipality of Črnomelj invested around €70,000, and the villagers — with their established habit of voluntary contributions — added about €7,000. The light was officially opened on the weekend in early October, with a cultural programme; the addresses by mayor Andrej Kavšek and community president Romana Husič confirmed what earlier years had proven: village infrastructure is a novel written by the municipality and the village together.

But the weightiest fact of the record is the quietest: during the construction, archaeological surveys were carried out, worth about €12,500. A village beneath whose fields lie the Celtic gold of the Pezdir farm and the sites by the Kolpa no longer digs blindly — every trench that takes a spade first asks the archaeologists. The results of these surveys are not yet public — the museum explicitly seeks them, which the modest scale of the construction makes all the more remarkable: rarely does so small a village investment carry an archaeological survey at all.

Two years later, in August 2025, the most damaged stretch of the public path was repaved by the same pattern of cooperation — 190 metres, some €35,000: the municipality for the asphalt, the local community for replacing the bedding. The sequence — bells, school, lighting, road — is the calendar of a village that arranges its own world: line by line and year by year.

The sequence has a prehistory, recorded by Radio Odeon twenty-four months earlier: in the autumn of 2021 the same combination lit up the hamlet of Brinsko selo. The works were again carried out by EVI of Črnomelj, archaeology was again part of the deal — this time the STIK Group from Ljubljana, at a cost of €11,931.60 within an investment of €46,987.81 — the two sides again shared the funding (the villagers and the Griblje local community €10,000, the rest from the municipality), and the handover again carried three names: mayor Andrej Kavšek, KS president Toni Brinc — a council member today, at the helm then — and the benefactor dr. Franc Brinc. Two projects, two years apart, one pattern: the village and the municipality light it with the same signature.

The current also keeps everyday records that chronicles rarely store: in December 2021 Elektro Ljubljana (the Novo mesto distribution unit, Metlika supervision office) switched off the GOR. GRIBLJE transformer station for two hours because of works on the distribution network — twenty addresses lost power, house numbers 3–15 with their A and B divisions and one address recorded simply as »BŠ«. A routine notice is in truth a rare documented micro-geography of the village network: it tells which windows share the same cable — a fact the museum chronicle does not otherwise write, and the grid archives keep only in technical drawings.

The village’s infrastructure calendar has an older page: on 5 September 2008 the Dolenjski list wrote ‘From Griblje nothing more into the Kolpa’ — the opening of a treatment plant by the Kolpa and a new sewerage system for 200–300 population equivalents, an investment of over a million euros whose European protocol required a presentation in the fire station itself; seventy per cent of the funds came from the EU, and mayor Andrej Fabjan hailed the project as a contribution to a cleaner Kolpa. Treatment plant 2008, public lighting 2023, asphalt 2025 — the same pattern three generations running: a village building its fortune piece by piece.

Since 2025 the story has also acquired a precise map of the grid, written by the cuts: in October 2025 Elektro Ljubljana cut TP GOR. GRIBLJE in one stroke — as many as 38 addresses, from GRIBLJE 1 A to 52 and BŠ; in June 2026 came the cut of outlet 2, named by Elektro itself: 'GOR.G.-VIKENDI' (addresses 1 A, 4 A, 4 G, 25 D and BŠ) — the weekend houses by the Kolpa; and in August 2026 the current vanished from the Šola outlet of the TP GRIBLJE station (30 A–48 and BŠ) — proof that besides GOR. GRIBLJE the village has a second transformer station, its branch by the school carrying a name of its own. Every cut is a blunt but irreplaceable census: it says which windows share the same cable — now we know they are divided across two stations and at least three named branches. And the lighting near the school has a birth date of its own: on 8 October 2021 the ribbon was cut by Dr Franc Brinc and local community president Toni Brinc with mayor Andrej Kavšek.

The museum seeks: the results of the lighting archaeology, a photograph of the opening, and a register of the village's first public lamp — where it burned before the current came.

exhibits.titleSi: Najboljša belokranjska pogača 44. Vinske vigredi — iz Gribelj
exhibits.titleEn: The best Bela krajina pogača of the 44th Vinska vigred — from Griblje
exhibits.summarySi: Na ocenjevanju belokranjske pogače pred 44. Vinsko vigredjo je zmagala Darinka Jerčinovič z »Kovačnice sreče« iz Gribelj, zbrala 79,38 točk — pogača, ki jo regija peče po receptih babic, je leta 2024 gribeljsko pečico pripeljala do najvišjega priznanja.
exhibits.summaryEn: At the judging of the Bela krajina pogača before the 44th Vinska vigred, Darinka Jerčinovič of the 'Kovačnica sreče' in Griblje won with 79.38 points — the flatbread the region bakes by its grandmothers' recipes carried a Griblje oven to the highest recognition in 2024.
exhibits.storySi:
Belokranjska pogača ni le jed — je seznam pravil na papirju: evropsko priznanje »bela krajina pogača« nosi recept, ki se peče skoraj izključno doma, po metliških, črnomaljskih in semiških kuhinjah. Vsako leto pred Vinsko vigredjo se v Metliki sreča ocenjevanje, ki izmed pogač izbere najboljšo — in leta 2024 je bila najboljša pogača iz Gribelj.

Zmagovalka je Darinka Jerčinovič, hiša po imenu »Kovačnica sreče«: 79,38 točk, objavljeno 25. aprila 2024, na pragu 44. Vinske vigredi. Zapis ima v zbirki svojo težo: gribeljska kuhinja je v zbirki že stala ob zgibanki belokranjske kuhinje — zdaj ima dokaz tudi o peki, ki je merilo za celotno regijo. Pogača je poleg tega sestrska šega pisanicam: tudi ona je bela, tudi na njo se riše — po njej pa je prepoznavna vasa ob Kolpi postala prepoznavna na metliškem prazničnem trgu.

Naslov pa je ostal doma tudi leta 2026: 21. aprila je v Hiši dobrot Bele krajine v Metliki komisija (pod RIC Bela krajina in Društvom kmečkih žena Metlika) ocenjevala pogače certificiranih proizvajalcev — in Darinka Jerčinovič je z 79 od 80 možnih točk spekla pogačo, ki je bila po zapisu »praktično brezhibna«: debelina testa, število zarezov, barva skorje, rahlost sredice, harmonija okusa. Po zmagi 2024 in medvladju Hiše dobrot (2025) je to drugi gribeljski naslov v treh letih — drugi poročevalec (Odeon ob Vinski vigredi) pa je dodal še presojo: vrhunska peka se »ne le ohranja, temveč pili do popolnosti«. Pogača, ki je v evropskem registru zaščitena do števila zarezov, ima v Gribljeh pečico, ki merilo regije zna držati.

Muzej išče: fotografijo pogače ali peke, recept, in zgodbo o tem, kako je pogača potovala iz gribeljske pečice na metliško ocenjevalno mizo.
exhibits.storyEn:
The Bela krajina pogača is not merely a dish — it is a list of rules on paper: the European recognition 'bela krajina pogača' carries a recipe baked almost exclusively at home, in the kitchens of Metlika, Črnomelj and Semič. Every year before the Vinska vigred festival Metlika hosts the judging that picks the best loaf among them — and in 2024 the best loaf came from Griblje.

The winner was Darinka Jerčinovič, a house called the 'Kovačnica sreče' — the forge of happiness: 79.38 points, announced on 25 April 2024, on the threshold of the 44th Vinska vigred. The record carries weight in this collection: Griblje's cooking already stood beside the Bela krajina cuisine spread — now it has proof of a bake that was the measure of the whole region. The pogača is, moreover, the sister custom of the pisanice: it, too, is white, and it, too, is drawn upon — and by it the village by the Kolpa became recognisable on Metlika's festive square.

The title stayed at home in 2026 as well: on 21 April, at the Hiša dobrot Bele krajine in Metlika, a jury (under RIC Bela krajina and the Metlika Farm Women's Society) judged the loaves of certified producers — and Darinka Jerčinovič, with 79 of the possible 80 points, baked a pogača recorded as 'practically flawless': the dough's thickness, the number of cuts, the crust's colour, the crumb's lightness, the harmony of taste. After the 2024 win and the interregnum of Hiša dobrot (2025), this is Griblje's second title in three years — and the second reporter (Odeon, at the Vinska vigred) added a verdict of its own: fine baking 'is not only preserved but honed to perfection'. The pogača, protected in the European register down to the number of cuts, has in Griblje an oven that knows how to hold the region's yardstick.

The museum seeks: a photograph of the loaf or of the baking, the recipe, and the story of how the pogača travelled from a Griblje oven to the Metlika judging table.

exhibits.titleSi: Dragojila Milek — Gregorčičeva »planinska roža« z očetovo domovijo v Gribljih
exhibits.titleEn: Dragojila Milek — Gregorčič's 'mountain flower', whose father's home was Griblje
exhibits.summarySi: Učiteljica in pesnica, rojena kot Karolina Milek, znana kot velika ljubezen pesnika Simona Gregorčiča — in hči očeta, ki je bil doma iz sosednjih Gribelj. Zadnjo službo je dobila 1888 v Podzemlju, župniji, ki ji pripada tudi gribeljska cerkev; tam je učila le nekaj mesecev, preden jo je odnesla bolezen.
exhibits.summaryEn: A teacher and poet, born Karolina Milek, known as the great love of the poet Simon Gregorčič — and the daughter of a father whose home was neighbouring Griblje. She received her last post in 1888 in Podzemelj, the parish to which the Griblje church also belongs; she taught there only a few months before illness carried her off.
exhibits.storySi:
Ta zapis se začne ne v Gribljih, ampak se tam vseskozi vrača. Dragojila Milek — rojena kot Karolina, 11. novembra 1850 v Zalogu pri Ljubljani, na Martinovo, v družini nižjega mestnega stražnika Petra Mileka in Katarine rojene Leban — je ena izmed najbolj znanih slovenskih učiteljic 19. stoletja in pesnica, ki jo je zgodovina najraje zapisovala ob drugem imenu: Simon Gregorčič, goriški slavček. In v njenem življenjepisu stoji stavek, ki povezuje to zgodbo z vasjo ob Kolpi: njen oče, ki si je kasneje v Ljubljani ustvaril svojo družino, je bil doma iz sosednjih Gribelj.

Šolala se je pri ljubljanskih uršulinkah, učiteljski izpit pa je opravila pri zasebni učiteljici Juliji Moosovi, saj učiteljišča za dekleta takrat še ni bilo. Govorila je nemško, francosko in italijansko, brala pa tudi v ruščini. Leta 1872 je kot prva učiteljica prišla v Kobarid, kjer je uvedla pouk ženskih ročnih del, vodila cerkveni pevski zbor, režirala na domačem odru in za prirodoslovca Frana Erjavca zbirala ljudske pesmi ter ljudska rastlinska imena. Tam je kot tajnica čitalnice spoznala kaplana Simona Gregorčiča. Sorodni duši sta se zbližali; ljubezen med njima je trajala dlje kot njuna bližina — Gregorčiča je kmalu zamenjala služba, župnik pa je premeščitev sam predlagal škofu. Junija 1873 mu je Milekova posvetila pesem Sloves; Gregorčič ji je odgovoril z pesmijo Ohrani Bog te v cveti, podpisano s psevdonimom Bojan, in ko jo je uglasbil Gustav Ipavec, je nastalo ime, ki danes poznajo vsi, ki poznajo Gregorčiča: Planinska roža.

Sama je objavljala pod psevdonimi: v Vrtcu kot Petrovna, v Ljubljanskem zvonu 1887 pa pesem Zgodnja cvetlica kot Črnogorka. Pisma je pisala pesniku Josipu Cimpermanu — del tega arhiva hrani Narodna in univerzitetna knjižnica. Poroka med duhovnikom in učiteljico ni bila možna: duhovnika je vezal celibat, učiteljice pa je poroka takrat odnesla pravico do poučevanja. Ko je leta 1888 podzemeljski ravnatelj Ivan Barle — učitelj, ki ga ta zbirka pozna tudi kot osebo, pri kateri so se pred 1889 šolali gribeljski otroci — enorazredno šolo v Podzemlju spremenil v dvorazrednico, se je Dragojila na lastno željo premeščila na Belo krajino. V podzemeljski šoli je stanovala in učila le nekaj mesecev: zbolela je za hudo tuberkulozo, bila upokojena in naslednje leto umrla v Ljubljani pri starših. Dolenjski list jo je tako v seriji Ljudje ob Kolpi 22. julija 2022 poslal domov za vedno — z opombo, da so njena pisma v veliki meri uničili domači, ker se je zgražalo nad ljubeznijo, ki ni smela biti.

Ob smrti so se je spomnili največji slovenski listi tistega časa; Dolenjski list pa ji je 1969 ob obnovljenem zanimanju za Gregorčiča posvetil kar dve objavi. Gribeljska nit zgodbe je tanka, a je dokumentirana s štirimi neodvisnimi viri: očetova domovija, podzemeljska služba v župniji gribeljske cerkve, ravnatelj Barle iz našega registra in narava, ki je po tej zbirki v Gribljih vedno nosila ime rože — planinske. Muzej išče: odlomek obeh Bačerjevih člankov iz Dolenjskega lista 1969, fotografijo podzemeljske šole tistega časa in zvezek pesmi, ki ga hrani NUK.
exhibits.storyEn:
This record does not begin in Griblje — it keeps returning there. Dragojila Milek — born Karolina on 11 November 1850 at Zalog near Ljubljana, on St Martin's day, into the family of a minor town constable, Peter Milek, and Katarina née Leban — is one of the best-known Slovene teachers of the 19th century and a poet whom history preferred to write down beside another name: Simon Gregorčič, the nightingale of Gorizia. And her biography contains the sentence that ties this story to the village on the Kolpa: her father, who later made his family in Ljubljana, was from neighbouring Griblje.

She was schooled with the Ursulines of Ljubljana and qualified for teaching with the private teacher Julija Moos, for there was no teacher-training college for girls in those days. She spoke German, French and Italian, and read Russian too. In 1872 she came to Kobarid as its first teacher, introducing classes in women's handwork, leading the church choir, directing on the local stage, and gathering folk songs and folk plant names for the naturalist Fran Erjavec. There, as secretary of the reading room, she met the curate Simon Gregorčič. Two kindred souls drew close; the love between them outlasted their proximity — a new post soon took Gregorčič away, and it was the parish priest himself who proposed the transfer to the bishop. In June 1873 Milek devoted to him the poem Sloves — The Farewell; Gregorčič answered with the poem Ohrani Bog te v cveti — God keep you in bloom — signed with the pseudonym Bojan, and when Gustav Ipavec set it to music it received the name everyone who knows Gregorčič knows today: Planinska roža — the mountain flower.

She herself published under pseudonyms: as Petrovna in Vrtec, and in the Ljubljanski zvon of 1887 the poem Zgodnja cvetlica — The early flower — as Črnogorka. She wrote letters to the poet Josip Cimperman — part of that archive is kept by the National and University Library. Marriage between a priest and a teacher was impossible: the priest was bound by celibacy, and in those days a teacher lost her right to teach by marrying. When in 1888 the Podzemelj head teacher Ivan Barle — the teacher whom this collection knows also as the man by whom Griblje's children learned before 1889 — raised the one-class school of Podzemelj to a two-class one, Dragojila transferred at her own request to Bela krajina. She lived in the Podzemelj school and taught only a few months: she fell gravely ill with tuberculosis, was pensioned off, and died the following year in Ljubljana at her parents' home. On 22 July 2022 the Dolenjski list, in its People by the Kolpa series, thus sent her home for good — with the note that her letters were largely destroyed by her family, which frowned upon a love that was not allowed to be.

At her death the leading Slovene papers of the day remembered her; the Dolenjski list devoted two items to her in 1969, when interest in Gregorčič was renewed. The Griblje thread of the story is thin, but it is documented by four independent witnesses: the father's home village, the Podzemelj post within the parish of the Griblje church, the head teacher Barle from our register, and the fact that in this region nature has always carried the name of a flower — a mountain one. The museum seeks: the text of both Bačer items in the Dolenjski list of 1969, a photograph of the Podzemelj school of that time, and the notebook of poems kept by the NUK.

exhibits.titleSi: Prof. dr. John Randolph Totter — biokemik, najmlajši sin Matička iz Gribelj
exhibits.titleEn: Prof. dr. John Randolph Totter — the biochemist, youngest son of Matiček of Griblje
exhibits.periodSi: 7. januar 1914 – 1. februar 2001 · Saragosa, Balmorhea, Oak Ridge
exhibits.periodEn: 7 January 1914 – 1 February 2001 · Saragosa, Balmorhea, Oak Ridge
exhibits.summarySi: Najmlajši od šestih otrok Jandrečega Matička (Matija Totter iz Gribelj) in Angležinje Agnes Smith: od otroškega kompleta za razcvetno analizo, podarjenega od duhovnika, do doktorata kemije in svetovno znanega biokemika v Nacionalnem laboratoriju Oak Ridge — vrednostni pečat Jandrečevega pravila, da so Tottrovi raje imeli knjigo kot plug.
exhibits.summaryEn: The youngest of the six children of Jandreč Matiček (Matija Totter of Griblje) and the Englishwoman Agnes Smith: from a child's blowpipe analysis kit, a gift from a priest, to a chemistry doctorate and a world-known biochemist at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory — the seal of the Jandreč rule that the Totters preferred the book to the plough.
exhibits.storySi:
Zbirka že hrani zapis o Jandreču Matičku, gribeljskem popisovalcu šeg, ki je končal v Teksasu, in o njegovi nečakinji Audrey, zvezdnici Hollywooda. Ta zapis dopolnjuje rodovnik z najmlajšo vejo: prof. dr. John Randolph Totter, najmlajši od šestih otrok Matije Tottre in Angležinje Agnes Smith iz Manchestra, se je rodil 7. januarja 1914 v Saragosi v Reeves County na Teksasu. Njegova starša sta se spoznala in poročila 1902 v Jolietu v Illinoisu — istem mestu z močno slovensko skupnostjo, kjer je živel tudi Janez Totter, oče Audrey. Družina je na Teksas prišla 1908, ko se je Matiček — ki je doma odšel prav zato, da ne bi bil kmet — združil prihranke z bratom Janezem in kupil farmo na zahodu Teksasa pri podjetju Balcomb, Moore and Rhea; iz teh treh imen je nastalo ime mestece Balmorhea, ki je postalo dom Tottrovih.

Otroštvo je oblikovala dva: sestra Mabel, učiteljica, ki je petletnega Johna vzela s sabo v šolo in mu pozneje omogočila študij v Laramieju, ter duhovnik Brocardus Eiken, ki je dečku podaril komplet za razcvetno analizo mineralov in ga vzel s sabo na potovanja za zanimivimi kamni. Sedem razredov je opravil v Saragosi, eno leto v Balmorhei, 1929 pa je maturiral pri 15 letih. Ker si ni mogel privoščiti risalne opreme za rudarsko inženirstvo, je izbral kemijo — in odkril dar za pametenje organskih formul, ki ga je poneslo v biokemijo. Bachelor 1934 in master 1935 na Univerzi v Wyomingu, doktorat kemije pa 1938 na Univerzi v Iowi; dan po promociji, 6. avgusta 1938, se je poročil z učiteljico Elizo »Betty« Van Sant.

Njegovo polje je bila biokemija, ustanova pa Nacionalni laboratorij Oak Ridge. Gribeljski viri v zbirki — rodopis o Matičku in Dolenjski list 2021 — mu pripisujeta še vodstvo raziskave Atomic Energy Commission o posledicah atomskih bomb nad Hirošimo in Nagasakijem ter sodelovanje z Institutom »Jožef Stefan«; o ustnem zgodovinskem zapisu, ki ga je 23. januarja 1995 posnel Oddelek za energijo ZDA, pa ETHW zgradi njegov življenjepis. Umrl je 1. februarja 2001. Po Županičevi opazki — »Jandrečim ne dišita plug in motika, pač pa imajo raje knjigo in gosli« — je bil John najčistejši dokaz: fant iz tekške ravnine, vendar z gribeljskim pravilom v hrbtenici. Muzej išče: osebne predmete in pisma iz arhiva Tottrovih, posnetek ustne zgodovine iz 1995 in fotografije, ki pokažejo, kako je teksaška domačija ohranila gribeljske navade.
exhibits.storyEn:
The collection already keeps the record of Jandreč Matiček, the recorder of customs from Griblje who ended in Texas, and of his niece Audrey, the star of Hollywood. This record adds the family tree's youngest branch: prof. dr. John Randolph Totter, the youngest of the six children of Matija Totter and the Englishwoman Agnes Smith of Manchester, was born on 7 January 1914 in Saragosa, in Reeves County, Texas. His parents met and married in 1902 in Joliet, Illinois — the same town with a strong Slovene community where Janez Totter, Audrey's father, lived. The family reached Texas in 1908, when Matiček — who had left home precisely to escape farming — pooled his savings with his brother Janez and bought a farm in West Texas through the firm of Balcomb, Moore and Rhea; from those three names grew the name of the little town of Balmorhea, which became the Totters' home.

Two figures shaped his childhood: his sister Mabel, a teacher, who took the five-year-old John along to school and later made his study in Laramie possible, and the priest Brocardus Eiken, who gave the boy a blowpipe analysis kit for minerals and took him along on his travels in search of interesting stones. He completed seven grades in Saragosa, one year in Balmorhea, and graduated in 1929 at the age of 15. Unable to afford the drafting equipment for mining engineering, he chose chemistry — and discovered a gift for remembering organic formulas, which carried him into biochemistry. A bachelor's in 1934 and a master's in 1935 at the University of Wyoming, and a chemistry doctorate in 1938 at the University of Iowa; the day after his defence, on 6 August 1938, he married the schoolteacher Eliza 'Betty' Van Sant.

His field was biochemistry, his institution the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The Griblje sources in this collection — the family record of Matiček and the Dolenjski list of 2021 — add to it the leadership of the Atomic Energy Commission's study of the consequences of the atomic bombs over Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the collaboration with the Jožef Stefan Institute; and it is from the oral-history interview recorded on 23 January 1995 by the United States Department of Energy that ETHW builds his biography. He died on 1 February 2001. By Županič's observation — 'the Jandreči have no taste for plough and hoe; they prefer the book and the fiddle' — John was the purest proof: a boy of the Texas plain, yet with the Griblje rule in his spine. The museum seeks: personal objects and letters from the Totter archive, the 1995 oral-history recording, and photographs showing how the Texas homestead kept the habits of Griblje.

exhibits.titleSi: Valentina Štrucelj — klarinetistka iz Gribelj, ki je ljubljansko zavrnitev pretvorila v odliko v Gradcu
exhibits.titleEn: Valentina Štrucelj — the clarinettist from Griblje who turned a Ljubljana rejection into a distinction in Graz
exhibits.periodSi: od 2010 po svetu · od 2007 v Švici · Glasbena šola konservatorij Bern
exhibits.periodEn: across the world since 2010 · in Switzerland since 2007 · Music school conservatory Bern
exhibits.summarySi: Gribeljčanka, ki se je note učila od sosednje deklice iz glasbene šole in po zavrnitvi Akademije za glasbo v Ljubljani z odliko diplomirala v Gradcu; danes je učiteljica klarineta na glasbeni šoli konservatorij v Bernu, prva klarinetistka Projekt simfoničnega orkestra in avtorica eksperimenta Current Density.
exhibits.summaryEn: A woman of Griblje who learned her notes from a neighbouring girl already at music school and, after being refused by the Academy of Music in Ljubljana, graduated with distinction in Graz; today she teaches clarinet at the music school conservatory in Bern, is the first clarinet of the Projekt symphonic orchestra, and the author of the experiment Current Density.
exhibits.storySi:
Zgodba, ki jo ta zapis hrani, se začne z otroško igračo: nekdo v Gribljih je Valentini Štrucelj za peti ali šesti rojstni dan podaril otroški sintetizator — in igračka je odločila poklic. Po posluhu je igrala nanj, ob nedeljah pa hodila k sosednji deklici, ki je že obiskovala glasbeno šolo, in se pri njej učila note. Ko je njeno igranje slišal družinski prijatelj, klarinetist, je svetoval glasbeno šolo; ravnatelj Glasbene šole Črnomelj Silvester Mihelčič ji je — ker oboo v Črnomlju nihče ni učil — predlagal klarinet. Od 5. razreda osnovne šole je hodila na glasbeno, po začetnih težavah pa se je v 7. razredu odločila: postala bo glasbenica. Glasbena nadarjenost v družini ni sama: sestrična Kristina Oberžan je uspešna pevka.

Srednjo glasbeno šolo je obiskovala v Ljubljani; že v 2. letniku se je odločila za študij v tujini. Edina od sošolcev je naredila sprejemne izpite na univerzo za glasbo v avstrijskem Gradcu — in po 4 letih študija diplomirala z odliko. Nasprotje zgodbe je grenko in poučno: na Akademijo za glasbo v Ljubljani so jo zavrnili z obrazložitvijo, da ji primanjkuje umetniškega talenta. Njena odgovor je kariera, ki se piše z odlikami: v Gradcu se je ob rednem študiju posvetila sodobni glasbi pri švicarskem profesorju, po srečanju s klarinetistom Ernestom Molinarjem pa nadaljevala v Bernu, kjer je zaključila pedagoški magisterij in — po Odeonu kot edina Slovenka — magistrski študij bas klarineta. Od leta 2007 živi v Švici; pred tem 4 leta v Avstriji.

Danes poučuje klarinet na Glasbeni šoli konservatorij v Bernu, igra komorno in eksperimentira: v baslu je sodelovala z ansamblom sodobne glasbe, ki ga je ustanovila Slovenka, z ansamblom Neufonia pa v netipični zasedbi tuba, klarinet in klavir igra klezmer, švicarsko narodno glasbo in svobodno improvizacijo. Eno leto je igrala v bernskem simfoničnem orkestru in ugotovila, da veliki orkestri, kjer ni eksperimentiranja, niso zanjo; v Projekt simfoničnem orkestru — kjer igra prvi klarinet — pa nastopa dvakrat letno z Beethovnom, Čajkovskim in Mozartom. Lani je v Ljubljani izšel album Current Density, ki ga je s kontrabasistom Sebastianom Rotzlerjem iz Biela posnela v Galeriji Škuc v okviru KUD Mreža — abstraktna, popolnoma odprta izvedba, ki je ne opiše nič drugega kot komunikacija dveh glasbenikov brez vnaprejšnjega dogovarjanja.

Ob 21. avgustu 2010, ko je Dolenjski list objavil njen intervju, je študij v Bernu šele končevala; 4. oktobra 2025 pa je Radio Odeon v seriji Belokranjci po svetu zapisal, da njena pot — in njena hčerka, ki ji doma posluša Pastirče mlado — rastejo naprej. Gribeljski sintetizator je zrasel v glasbenico, ki bernske učence uči po poti, ki je za vsakega najlažja: »Vsak človek je unikaten. Pri vsakem posebej moram iskati pot, ki je zanj najlažja, da se nauči igrati.« Muzej išče: fotografijo domačega nastopa, program metliških Večerov na gradu 2010 in posnetek koncerta v Galeriji Škuc.
exhibits.storyEn:
The story this record keeps begins with a toy: someone in Griblje gave Valentina Štrucelj a child's synthesizer for her fifth or sixth birthday — and the toy decided the vocation. She played it by ear, and on Sundays she went to a neighbouring girl who already attended the music school, learning her notes from her. When a family friend, a clarinettist, heard her play, he advised music school; the head of the Črnomelj music school, Silvester Mihelčič — since nobody in Črnomelj taught the oboe — proposed the clarinet. From the 5th grade of primary school she attended the music school, and after initial struggles in the 7th grade she decided: she would become a musician. Musical talent is not alone in the family: her cousin Kristina Oberžan is a successful singer.

She attended secondary music school in Ljubljana; already in her 2nd year she decided on study abroad. Alone among her classmates she passed the entrance exams at the university of music in Graz, Austria — and after 4 years of study graduated with distinction. The counterpoint of the story is bitter and instructive: the Academy of Music in Ljubljana rejected her with the explanation that she lacked artistic talent. Her answer is a career written in distinctions: in Graz she devoted herself, beside her regular studies, to contemporary music with a Swiss professor, and after meeting the clarinettist Ernesto Molinari she continued in Bern, where she completed a pedagogical master's and — by Radio Odeon, as the only Slovene — a master's in bass clarinet. She has lived in Switzerland since 2007; 4 years in Austria before that.

Today she teaches clarinet at the music school conservatory in Bern, plays chamber music and experiments: in Basel she worked with a contemporary-music ensemble founded by a Slovene woman, and with the Neufonia ensemble — in the unusual scoring of tuba, clarinet and piano — she plays klezmer, Swiss folk music and free improvisation. For one year she played in the Bern symphonic orchestra and concluded that large orchestras, where there is no experimenting, are not for her; in the Projekt symphonic orchestra — where she plays first clarinet — she performs twice a year with Beethoven, Tchaikovsky and Mozart. Recently the album Current Density appeared, recorded in the Škuc Gallery within the KUD Mreža with the double-bassist Sebastian Rotzler of Biel — an abstract, entirely open performance that nothing describes better than two musicians communicating without any prior agreement.

On 21 August 2010, when the Dolenjski list published her interview, she was only finishing her studies in Bern; on 4 October 2025 Radio Odeon, in its Bela krajina people around the world series, recorded that her path — and her little daughter, who at home listens to Pastirče mlado — keep growing. The Griblje synthesizer grew into a musician who teaches Bern's pupils by the path easiest for each: 'Every human being is unique. For each one I must seek the path that makes learning to play easiest.' The museum seeks: a photograph of a home performance, the programme of the Metlika Evenings at the castle of 2010, and a recording of the Škuc Gallery concert.

exhibits.titleSi: TULV/Griblje/Ma57_01 — Tulski virus, ki za vedno nosi ime vasi
exhibits.titleEn: TULV/Griblje/Ma57_01 — the Tula virus that carries the village's name forever
exhibits.summarySi: Leta 2001 je bila v Gribljih ulovljena poljska voluharica, iz katere so raziskovalci Instituta za mikrobiologijo Medicinske fakultete prvič molekularno dokazali Tulski virus (TULV) v voluharjih v Sloveniji. Sev nosi ime TULV/Griblje/Ma57_01 — od 2009 zapisan v mednarodni bazi GenBank, tako da je ime vasi postalo del znanstvene nomenklature.
exhibits.summaryEn: In 2001 a common vole was caught in Griblje from whose lungs researchers of the Institute of Microbiology of the Medical Faculty provided the first molecular evidence of the Tula virus (TULV) in Microtus voles in Slovenia. The strain bears the name TULV/Griblje/Ma57_01 — recorded in the international GenBank database since 2009, so that the village's name has become part of scientific nomenclature.
exhibits.storySi:
Malo je naselij, ki imajo svoje ime vpisano v mednarodne baze podatkov o virusih. Griblje imajo — in to po poti, ki je bila povsem znanstvena. Zgodba se začne leta 2001, ko je na terenu v Gribljih prišel v roke raziskovalcem primerek poljske voluharice (Microtus arvalis), malega glodalca mokrih travnikov ob Kolpi. Iz njegovih pljuč je ekipa Instituta za mikrobiologijo in imunologijo Medicinske fakultete v Ljubljani molekularno dokazala Tulski virus (Tula orthohantavirus, TULV) — virus, poimenovan po mestu Tula v Rusiji, ki pri ljudeh sicer povzroča blažjo obliko hemoragične mrzlice z renalnim sindromom, v naravi pa ga prenašajo glodavci.

Najdba je bila znanstveno prelomna: prvo molekularno dokazilo o Tulskem virusu v voluharjih (rod Microtus) v Sloveniji. Oznaka seva — TULV/Griblje/Ma57_01 — sledi mednarodni konvenciji: ime najdišča, oznaka nosilca in številka živali z letom (razlaga kode je muzejska, ne izpričana iz vira). Sekvenci segmentov L in S sta bili deponirani 1. decembra 2008 v mednarodno bazo GenBank pod številkama FJ495099 in FJ495093; kot prijavitelji so zapisani M. Korva, D. Duh in T. Avšič-Županc (Univerza v Ljubljani, Inštitut za mikrobiologijo in imunologijo, Zaloška 4).

Leta 2009 je v reviji Virus Research (letn. 144, št. 1–2, str. 318–322; PMID 19410611) izšel članek Korvare, Duha, Puterleta, Trilarja in Zupančeve z naslovom First molecular evidence of Tula hantavirus in Microtus voles in Slovenia — z gribeljskim sevom kot enim od ključnih dokazov. Leta 2013 pa je mednarodna ekipa v vplivni reviji Emerging Infectious Diseases (CDC, letn. 19, št. 11; DOI 10.3201/eid1911.130421) gribeljski sev uporabila v filogenetski primerjavi evropskih hantavirusov — »Griblje/Ma57/01 (FJ495099)« tako stoji med slovenskimi sevi ob Hodos, Sred ob Dravi in Sestrže v objavljeni drevesni razvejitvi.

Po vzoru ribe Alburnus sava, vrste opisane iz Kolpe, ta zapis nadaljuje nit »vas v znanosti«: leta 2001 je ta vas dala ime sevu, ki ga bo svetovna literatura citirala še desetletja. Muzej išče: laboratorijski dnevnik terenske izprave 2001, točno lokacijo ulova znotraj vasi, fotografijo primerka in objavo o izpravi v lokalnem glasilu.
exhibits.storyEn:
Few settlements have their name written into the international virus databases. Griblje does — by a path that was purely scientific. The story begins in 2001, when a common vole (Microtus arvalis), the small rodent of the wet meadows along the Kolpa, was caught in the field at Griblje. From its lungs the team of the Institute of Microbiology and Immunology of the Medical Faculty in Ljubljana proved molecularly the presence of the Tula virus (Tula orthohantavirus, TULV) — a virus named after the town of Tula in Russia, which in humans causes the milder form of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and lives in nature among rodents.

The finding was a scientific breakthrough: the first molecular evidence of the Tula virus in Microtus voles in Slovenia. The strain's designation — TULV/Griblje/Ma57_01 — follows the international convention: the site's name, the host's code and the animal's number with the year (the reading of the code is the museum's, not attested by a source). The sequences of the L and S segments were deposited on 1 December 2008 into the international GenBank database under the numbers FJ495099 and FJ495093; the submitters recorded are M. Korva, D. Duh and T. Avšič-Županc (University of Ljubljana, Institute of Microbiology and Immunology, Zaloška 4).

In 2009 the journal Virus Research (vol. 144, no. 1–2, pp. 318–322; PMID 19410611) published the paper by Korva, Duh, Puterle, Trilar and Zupanc titled First molecular evidence of Tula hantavirus in Microtus voles in Slovenia — with the Griblje strain as one of the key proofs. In 2013 an international team in the influential journal Emerging Infectious Diseases (CDC, vol. 19, no. 11; DOI 10.3201/eid1911.130421) used the Griblje strain in a phylogenetic comparison of European hantaviruses — 'Griblje/Ma57/01 (FJ495099)' thus stands among the Slovene strains beside Hodos, Sred ob Dravi and Sestrže in the published branching of the tree.

In the wake of the fish Alburnus sava, the species described from the Kolpa, this record continues the thread of 'the village in science': in 2001 this village gave its name to a strain that the world's literature will cite for decades. The museum seeks: the field notebook of the 2001 expedition, the exact location of the catch within the village, a photograph of the specimen, and any report of the expedition in a local paper.

exhibits.titleSi: Cryptachaea riparia — pajek, katerega prvi slovenski primerki so bili zabeleženi tudi ob ribniku pri Gribljih
exhibits.titleEn: Cryptachaea riparia — the spider whose first Slovene specimens were recorded also by the pond at Griblje
exhibits.periodSi: 29. julij 2001 · ribnik SZ od vasi Griblje
exhibits.periodEn: 29 July 2001 · the pond NW of the village of Griblje
exhibits.summarySi: V nacionalnem registru pajkov Slovenije (Araneae Sloveniae, ZooKeys 474, 2015) je vrsta Cryptachaea riparia z zvezdico označena kot nova za slovensko favno; med primerki, s katerimi je vrsta vpisana v seznam, je tudi samec z ribnika SZ od Gribelj — 29. 7. 2001, ujel in določil arahnolog Rok Kostanjšek.
exhibits.summaryEn: In the national register of Slovene spiders (Araneae Sloveniae, ZooKeys 474, 2015) the species Cryptachaea riparia is marked with an asterisk as new to the Slovene fauna; among the specimens by which the species entered the list is also a male from the pond NW of Griblje — 29 July 2001, collected and determined by the arachnologist Rok Kostanjšek.
exhibits.storySi:
Pajki so skromen vir vaške zgodovine — ampak prav ena od mikro-zgodb te vrste vpisuje Griblje v nacionalno znanstveno dokumentacijo. Leta 2015 je v odprto-dostopni reviji ZooKeys (letn. 474; DOI 10.3897/zookeys.474.8474; PMID 25632258) izšel Araneae Sloveniae, nacionalni seznam vrst pajkov, ki sta ga pripravila arahnolog Rok Kostanjšek in Matjaž Kuntner. Seznam ima jasno pravilo za zvezdice: vrste, ki jih za slovensko favno doslej niso zabeležili, so označene z zvezdico, ob njih pa so navedeni opisi najdišč, geografski podatki, datumi zbiranja ter podatki o zbiratelju in določevalcu.

Med zvezdicami je tudi Cryptachaea riparia (Blackwall, 1834) — majhna kroglastnica iz družine Theridiidae, vrsta, vezana na bregove in vodna okolja, kot pravi njeno ime (riparia = obrežna). Med primerki, s katerimi je vrsta vpisana v seznam, stoji zapis: »1♂ — Pond Ribnik NW of village Griblje; 45°34,56′ N, 15°17,01′ E, 150 m n. m.; 29. 7. 2001; leg. & det. Kostanjšek R.« — samec z ribnika SZ od vasi Griblje, ujet 29. julija 2001. Koordinata 45,576 N / 15,283 E ustreza vaškemu ribniku na zgornjem koncu vasi — istemu ribniku, ki ga zbirka pozna iz lastnega zapisa (MVG-016).

Gribeljski primerek je med najzgodnejšimi dokumentiranimi primerki vrste v seznamu — starejši je samo cerkniški iz 30. 7. 2000; gribeljski je zato eden izmed prvih primerkov, s katerimi je Cryptachaea riparia postala del slovenske favne. Zgodba ima tudi poetično simetrijo: vrsta obrežnih pajkov je prišla v nacionalni seznam z brega ribnika, ki vodi vodo vasi — in z očmi muzeja je to prvi zapis o nevretenčarju iz same vasi. Muzej išče: fotografijo vrste (vir je seznam brez slik), laboratorijski dnevnik zbiratelja in morebitne starejše zapise vrste iz arhiva Polenčevih določitev.
exhibits.storyEn:
Spiders are a modest source of village history — yet one of the micro-stories of this kind writes Griblje into the national scientific documentation. In 2015 the open-access journal ZooKeys (vol. 474; DOI 10.3897/zookeys.474.8474; PMID 25632258) published Araneae Sloveniae, the national checklist of spider species prepared by the arachnologist Rok Kostanjšek and Matjaž Kuntner. The checklist has a clear rule for asterisks: species not yet recorded for the Slovene fauna are marked with an asterisk, accompanied by descriptions of the collecting sites, geographic data, dates of collection, and the data of the collector and the determining authority.

Among the asterisks is Cryptachaea riparia (Blackwall, 1834) — a small comb-footed spider of the family Theridiidae, a species bound to banks and watery places, as its name says (riparia = of the riverbank). Among the specimens by which the species entered the list stands the entry: '1♂ — Pond Ribnik NW of village Griblje; 45°34.56′ N, 15°17.01′ E, 150 m a.s.l.; 29.7.2001; leg. & det. Kostanjšek R.' — a male from the pond north-west of the village of Griblje, caught on 29 July 2001. The coordinate 45.576 N / 15.283 E corresponds to the village pond at the upper end of the village — the same pond the collection knows from its own record (MVG-016).

The Griblje specimen is among the earliest documented specimens of the species in the list — only the Cerknica one of 30 July 2000 is older; the Griblje one is thus among the first specimens by which Cryptachaea riparia became part of the Slovene fauna. The story has a poetic symmetry too: a species of bank spiders entered the national list from the bank of the pond that leads the village its water — and with the museum's eyes this is the first record of an invertebrate from the village itself. The museum seeks: a photograph of the species (the source is a checklist without images), the collector's laboratory notebook, and any older records of the species from the archive of Polenec's determinations.

exhibits.titleSi: Poletje tranzita — ko je obvoz peljal skozi vas
exhibits.titleEn: The summer of transit — when the detour ran through the village
exhibits.periodSi: 19. maj → poletje 2025 · lokalna cesta skozi Griblje
exhibits.periodEn: 19 May → the summer of 2025 · the local road through Griblje
exhibits.summarySi: Od 19. maja 2025 so bili vaščani Gribelj izpostavljeni okrepljenemu tranzitnemu prometu: vozniki kljub uradnemu obvozu skozi Dolenjce — zaradi rekonstrukcije mostu čez Lahinjo v Gradcu — množično uporabljali lokalno cesto skozi vas. Dolenjski list je zapisal: »Na cesti skozi Griblje nevarnost preži na vsakem koraku.«
exhibits.summaryEn: From 19 May 2025 the villagers of Griblje were exposed to increased transit traffic: despite the official detour through Dolenjce — because of the reconstruction of the bridge over the Lahinja at Gradac — drivers used the local road through the village en masse. The Dolenjski list wrote: 'On the road through Griblje danger lurks at every step.'
exhibits.storySi:
Vas ob Kolpi je bila vse do obvoza tranzitna cesta — in ko si je poletje 2025 glavno pot vzelo za popravilo, se je stari vzorec za nekaj mesecev vrnil. 19. maja 2025 se je začela rekonstrukcija mostu čez Lahinjo v Gradcu; uradni obvoz je vodil skozi Dolenjce, vozniki pa so si množično skrajšali pot čez lokalno cesto skozi Griblje. Vas, ki ji je zadnja desetletja mir vrnil pešce in kolesarje, je za eno poletje znova postala prevozna povezava.

Dolenjski list je 11. julija 2025 objavil članek z naslovom »Na cesti skozi Griblje nevarnost preži na vsakem koraku«; meta opis članka stanje povzame: »Od 19. maja so vaščani Gribelj izpostavljeni okrepljenemu tranzitnemu prometu, saj vozniki kljub uradnemu obvozu skozi Dolenjce zaradi rekonstrukcije mostu čez reko Lahinjo v Gradcu množično uporabljajo lokalno cesto skozi njihovo naselje.« Zgodba je mikro-zgodovina vaške ceste: promet, ki ga je vaški spomin vedno poznal kot senca ob obvozu, se je vrnil kot vsakdanji zvok pod okni.

Zapis ta mesec zgodovine vasi dokumentira iz muzejske perspektive: ni to zgodba o gradnji, ampak o vsakdanjem odzivu vasi na promet, ki je prišel brez povabila. Je tudi opomin, da sta obvoz in most v Gradcu del istega vaškega prostora — »mimo vasi« pomeni »skoznjo«, takoj ko glavna pot odpove. Muzej išče: fotografije prometa poleti 2025, izjave KS Griblje ali Turističnega društva, datum odprtja rekonstruiranega mostu in morebitne peticije vaščanov.
exhibits.storyEn:
The village on the Kolpa was a transit road until the bypass came — and when the summer of 2025 took the main road away for repairs, the old pattern returned for a few months. On 19 May 2025 the reconstruction of the bridge over the Lahinja at Gradac began; the official detour led through Dolenjce, but drivers shortened their path en masse over the local road through Griblje. The village, to which the last decades of quiet had returned its pedestrians and cyclists, became once more a traffic link for one summer.

On 11 July 2025 the Dolenjski list published a piece titled 'Na cesti skozi Griblje nevarnost preži na vsakem koraku' — On the road through Griblje danger lurks at every step; the article's meta description sums up the state: 'From 19 May the villagers of Griblje have been exposed to increased transit traffic, as drivers, despite the official detour through Dolenjce because of the reconstruction of the bridge over the Lahinja at Gradac, use the local road through their settlement en masse.' The story is the micro-history of the village road: the traffic that the village's memory always knew as the shadow beside the bypass returned as an everyday sound under the windows.

The record documents this chapter of the village's history from the museum's perspective: it is not a story of construction, but of the village's everyday response to traffic that arrived uninvited. It is also a reminder that the bypass and the bridge at Gradac belong to the same village space — 'past the village' means 'through it' the moment the main road fails. The museum seeks: photographs of the traffic in the summer of 2025, statements by the Griblje local community or the Tourist Society, the date of the reconstructed bridge's opening, and any petitions of the villagers.
